provider.name: eBird
provider.organization_type: global bird observation, checklist, taxonomy, media, distribution, abundance, and citizen-science platform
provider.description: eBird is a global bird observation and citizen-science platform operated by the Cornell Lab of Ornithology. It manages checklists, species observations, effort and protocol metadata, taxonomy, hotspots, locations, media, regional summaries, research datasets, APIs, and modeled status-and-trends products.
institutional_context: Global eBird partners, reviewers, and regional networks

purpose.summary: This file is a crawl-ready source catalog for collecting eBird documentation, checklist and observation guidance, taxonomy, locations, hotspots, data-quality rules, sensitive-species policy, media licensing, bulk datasets, science products, APIs, citation instructions, and legal context.
purpose.authoritative_notice: eBird, the Cornell Lab of Ornithology, and Macaulay Library remain authoritative for observation records, taxonomy, media, data products, APIs, licenses, citation, terms, and contact information.

notes: Verify the current API documentation location, key requirements, limits, paging, response fields, and deprecations.
Do not store API keys or account credentials in this manifest.
Distinguish API observations from bulk EBD and Sampling Event Data products.
Capture species codes, region codes, hotspot identifiers, checklist identifiers, date semantics, and sensitive-data behavior.
Capture exact official legal wording before normalizing rights metadata.
Separate checklist and observation data, media assets, bulk datasets, API responses, and modeled products.
Preserve sensitive-species obscuration, private-location restrictions, contributor attribution, media licenses, and dataset citations.
Do not infer rights to media from rights to observation metadata.
Do not expose exact coordinates or locality details for records intentionally obscured by eBird.
Seed URLs are best-effort and were not live-verified in this session.
The acquisition program should update retrieval, content, review, and verification fields in place.
Some support article identifiers, science pages, API documentation paths, or status endpoints may move; preserve redirect and failure metadata.
Do not recursively crawl every checklist, species page, hotspot, region, map tile, media asset, or observation when the task is documentation acquisition.
Do not store eBird API keys, passwords, cookies, OAuth tokens, account credentials, or session credentials in this JSON file.
Observation metadata, checklists, media, bulk datasets, API responses, taxonomy, and modeled science products may carry different rights.
Always preserve checklist identifiers, taxonomy version, species code, protocol, effort, review state, sensitive-data treatment, license, citation, and source provenance.
